A series of small chirps and barks are heard as a sleek creature warily steps out from the quiet woods upon a snow covered glade. 
Clinging to its gray fur are an assortment of young, unrelated to the giant marsupial, yet she protectively guards them all the same. 
While widely spread across the island, they are a dwindling species, recent generations have been suffering from a low birth rate. To 
quell their matronly instincts, some female omaterssum will be seen adopting the young of different wayward creatures, those who lost 
their herd or fallen from their nest. While the females are seen to be fi ercely protective, the males on the other hand will go out of their 
way to slaughter any young not of their kin, further dividing the two sexes and fracturing the chances for the omaterssum to survive.

Adopted Litter When encountering an omaterssum, roll 1d4 and 
select that number of Young that originate from the biome that 
the omaterssum is currently in (each biome entry has a Young 
section, select creatures that make sense for the scenario). Make a 
separate roll for any other omaterssum and track which Adopted 
Litter belongs to which. Th e Adopted Litter attempt to remain 
close to their omaterssum parent and treat it and other Adopted 
Litter creatures as an ally. Th e Adopted Litter have Advantage 
on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of the Adopted 
Litter’s allies is within 5 ft. of the creature and the ally doesn’t have 
the Incapacitated condition. Any Adopted Litter residing in the 
omaterssum’s pouch has Total Cover against attacks and other 
effects outside the omaterssum.

Encountering Th ough few in number, this opportunistic 
omnivore can be found in all reaches of Sol’Kesh, from 
swimming along the Strands for clams, to shallow delves into 
the Umbrawells. Preferring the relative safety of the colder 
climes, they are most likely found in the conifer covered Last 
Bloom Wealdwoods prowling the higher altitudes that encircle 
the Splitspine mountains.
Commanding Call Th e omaterssum calls its Adopted Litter to 
harass a target within 30 ft.. Dexterity Saving Th row: DC 14, target 
creature within 5 ft. of an Adopted Litter creature. Failure: Th e 
target takes 7 (2d6) Piercing damage for every Adopted Litter 
creature within 5 ft. of it. 
Prehensile Tail Dexterity Saving Th row: DC 13, Medium or smaller 
Prone creature the omaterssum can see within 10 ft. Failure: Th e 
target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13).
Creature Collaborator • Bryant "Jenks" Jenkins
This large marsupial female uses its pouch to 
safeguard either their own offspring or adopted 
young during long migrations across the island 
A wayward vinnirex pup stares out 
timidly from the protective forelimb 
of the motherly beast that guards it
With a long, low to the ground 
lithe body, the omaterssum is 
capable of weaving between trees 
in and out of the underbrush to 
rush through the Wealdwoods 
at speeds many other creatures 
cannot hope to match 
A calitross fledgling clings onto the long warm 
fur, enjoying its vantage point on the large 
mammal that rescued it from the cold ground 
days earlier
